proof:
For a point $x$ in a new fiber at $z<0$, fix any facet normal $u$ of $T$ and choose $x_1\in T$ with $u\cdot x_1=h_T(u)$. The points $(z,x)$ and $(1,x_1)$ have a strict convex combination with base $0$, and its continuous coordinate belongs to $T$. Applying the facet inequality and canceling the second term gives $u\cdot x\le h_T(u)$. All facets together give $x\in T$. Reflection of the base coordinate gives the other side.

At the two exposed old bases, ordinary depth equals ordinary depth in the own fiber by 2acc8bc803acf1c0. Its centroid depth is $4|T|/9$. For the minimizing directions, a line through the centroid cuts off a one-vertex triangle on one side, with vertex functional values proportional to $1,-s,-t$, where $s,t\ge0$ and $s+t=1$. Its area fraction is $1/[(1+s)(1+t)]$, which lies between $4/9$ and $1/2$ and attains $4/9$ only when $s=t=1/2$. The complementary side has fraction at least $1/2$. Hence the minimizing normals are exactly positive multiples of $\lambda_j-1/3$, where $\lambda_j$ is the barycentric coordinate of the captured vertex. A pure-base cap pays the entire own fiber and cannot be active. A cap containing the centroid strictly can be shifted to pass through it and strictly reduce its own cap mass if the continuous normal is nonzero, since the centroid is interior; so every active cap passes through the mark.

At base zero an active cap has margin $az+\lambda_j(x)-1/3$ after positive scaling. Its own mass is $4|T|/9$ and the other fiber must contribute zero, requiring $a\le-2/3$ because $\max_T(\lambda_j-1/3)=2/3$. The minimum on $T$ is $-1/3$. Therefore at $z\le-1$ the margin is at least $1/3$ for all $x\in T$. Reflection gives the right assertion. The unique ordinary simplex centroid maximum, or the vertex cap bound away from the centroid, gives original global raw maximum $4|T|/9$ and total mass $2|T|$. Finally if the new law has left and right probabilities $L,R$, the corresponding source scores are at least $L,R$, and $\max(L,R)\ge1/2$.
statement: Let $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a nondegenerate triangle with centroid $0$, and use the product body $[0,1]\times T$ with integer base coordinate. Any convex extension preserving the two original fibers has its fibers at every integer $z\le-1$ and $z\ge2$ contained in $T$. Every ordinary active cap at $(0,0)$ captures every such preserving birth point on the left, and every active cap at $(1,0)$ captures every such point on the right, with signed margin at least $1/3$ after the cap's continuous functional is scaled to a barycentric margin. Consequently any preserving probability law on new sites has maximum of the two old source capture scores at least $1/2$, for every choice of probability mixtures of active caps at those sources. The old normalized maximum is $2/9$.
title: An ordinary two-triangle obstruction to low-capture fiber birth
